about: Alert Verification Engine settings (backend/soc/verify.py). Users, zones and maintenance tickets are NOT repeated here: they are read from the log folder's assets.yaml / maintenance.yaml.
high_risk_why: An alert this severe is never dismissed: the incident is at least 'suspicious'.
never_benign_why: Credential theft, privileged group change, pass-the-hash, ransomware/backup deletion, exfiltration, log clearing and operator-imported indicators: never benign, whoever did them.
suspicious_min_concerns_why: Two independent warning signs (compromised account, unknown address, forbidden zone traffic, several attack stages) make an incident 'suspicious' even without a high-risk rule.

inconclusive_when.why: Missing evidence (silent source, low confidence) is never proof of normal behaviour: at best 'inconclusive'. Evidence from one source only is 'inconclusive' unless an authorized activity below covers it.

shared_host_roles_why: Machines every member of staff may use; any other machine needs to be the user's own (home) machine, or the user must be a privileged admin working from the jump host.

authorized_activities.name: Known user mistypes the password, then logs on
authorized_activities.why: A known, non-compromised user from their own machine to a machine they may use; nothing else happened afterwards.

authorized_activities.name: Linux admin opens a root shell from the jump host
authorized_activities.why: Daily administration by the Linux admin account during working hours.

authorized_activities.name: Helpdesk changes membership of a normal group
authorized_activities.why: Helpdesk may add colleagues to non-privileged groups on the directory servers; a privileged group (PRIV-001) is never covered.
